skills.name: Common application software 1: word processors and spreadsheets

note.text:
Application software helps users do particular tasks.
• Word processor (e.g. Microsoft Word, LibreOffice Writer): letters, reports, CVs; features: formatting, spell check, tables, mail merge, headers and footers.
• Spreadsheet (e.g. Microsoft Excel, LibreOffice Calc): data in rows and columns of cells; formulas and functions calculate automatically; charts; sorting.
Cells have references such as B3 (column B, row 3). Formulas start with =: =B2*C2, =SUM(B2:B6), =AVERAGE(C2:C10), =MAX(…), =MIN(…).

sections.heading: Software for tasks
sections.text:
Application software lets users do jobs on a computer: write, calculate, present, draw, browse. System software (like the operating system) runs the computer itself.
Two of the most used applications are the word processor and the spreadsheet.

sections.heading: Word processors
Spreadsheets
sections.text:
Microsoft Excel or LibreOffice Calc arrange data in a grid of cells. Each cell has a reference: column letter + row number, such as {'B3'}.
Formulas start with = and recalculate automatically when data changes: ={'B2'}*{'C2'} (multiply), =SUM({'B2'}:{'B6'}) (add a range), =AVERAGE({'C2'}:{'C10'}), =MAX(…), =MIN(…).
Spreadsheets also sort data and draw charts: ideal for budgets, sales records and class marks.

mistake.why: The colon means 'from … to …': every cell in the range.

worked_example.problem: Cells {'B2'}, {'B3'} and {'B4'} contain {a}, {b} and {c}. What does =SUM({'B2'}:{'B4'}) display?
steps: SUM adds every cell from {'B2'} to {'B4'}.

cards.idea: A word processor is for documents; a spreadsheet is for calculations with data.
Spreadsheet formulas start with = and update automatically.
A cell reference names a column letter and a row number.

questions.prompt: Cells {'A1'} to {'A4'} contain {a}, {b}, {c} and {d}. What does =SUM({'A1'}:{'A4'}) display?

misconceptions.explain: {'A1'}:{'A4'} means all cells from {'A1'} to {'A4'}, not just the two ends.

solution: SUM adds all the cells from {'A1'} to {'A4'}.

questions.prompt: {'B2'} holds the price {p} FCFA and {'C2'} the quantity {q}. What does ={'B2'}*{'C2'} display?
Cells {'D2'} to {'D5'} hold the marks {a}, {b}, {c} and {d}. What does =AVERAGE({'D2'}:{'D5'}) display?

misconceptions.explain: That is the SUM. AVERAGE divides by the number of cells.

solution: AVERAGE adds the four marks and divides by {4}.
where: max(max(a, b), max(c, d)) != (a + b + c + d) / 4
